name: iorasglach

sources: McKay, John G. More West Highland Tales. Vol. 2. Scottish Anthropological and Folklore Society. Edinburgh: Oliver and Boyd, 1969, 496.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Iorasglach is a Scottish folkloric character. The name also appears as iorsglach-úrlair. She is a beggarly woman in threadbare clothing. Some Highland folktales cast her as a seer. She strikes the ground where she sits before she speaks her prophecies. She delivers these warnings to the lord and the court. Some scholars see in her a faint folk memory of a Celtic or pre-Celtic ritual of divination.
